rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.2-2.3 and 3 report a two-year rain-fed field experiment (winter wheat vs spring maize, with and without 160 kg N) measuring soil respiration, Q10, soil temperature/moisture, yield and root biomass in the semi-arid Loess Plateau.
rows.notes: The study contains no drip irrigation, no irrigation at all (rain-fed plots), no emitter spacing, irrigation scheduling or fertigation uniformity. It examines crop type and broadcast urea N fertilization effects on soil respiration and its temperature sensitivity (Q10). It reports yield increases with N fertilization but nothing about management precision of drip systems constraining productivity. Technology and effect in the passage are not addressed; apparent miscitation.

notes: Full text appears complete. The study is a primary field experiment on soil respiration Q10 under wheat/maize and N fertilization in rain-fed conditions; it has no relation to drip irrigation management precision.
